task: Phase 01 of the kernel architecture repair plan: contain unsafe paths (domain-class zero-copy grants, non-RV64 Tier-2 admission, warm snapshot) and capture behavioural baselines without changing the public ABI.
acceptanceCriteria: RV64 Tier-2 native launch and copied IPC still work; every domain-backed grant attempt fails closed before a PTE/frame is published; AArch64/x86_64 Tier-2 admission denies until phase 02 proves the ordered switch; Tier-1 SAS grants remain functional.
Snapshot reports unavailable with no disk write and no restore; cold boot and the shell/Supervisor snapshot contract are unchanged.
Pre-patch baseline identifies the exact feature/architecture image, and the unsafe behaviour fails before the patch instead of being relabelled as a pass.
publicContracts: libs/api and libs/types are untouched (Law 1): no new syscall, opcode, error or struct field.

Grant* result conventions preserved per operation: GrantAlloc/GrantRegister denial = Ok(0) (the cell wrapper decodes any nonzero return as a grant id), GrantSlice denial = Ok(usize::MAX), share/free/unregister denial = the established nonzero failure.
Syscall::Snapshot keeps SupervisorCap + SyscallError::Unknown and the shell/Supervisor 'unavailable' reply.
blastRadius: Tier-1 SAS grant, VFS lease and DMA paths (must be byte-for-byte behaviourally unchanged; proved by the grant-gate fixture's SAS leg)
Tier-2 admission on all three architectures (AArch64/x86_64 now deny by policy)
Snapshot capture/restore on every block-capable board (now gated by feature `snapshot-qualified`)
cells/tests/tier2-smoke + tier2_fault_isolation integration expectations (grant leg becomes a denial assertion)
scoutSummary: Domain grants reach the shared repo through six syscall arms plus GrantDma; the ungated path publishes USER PTEs in the SAS root for domain owners, maps receiver pages RW regardless of shared_to rights, and revokes only through the caller's own root. Non-RV64 Tier-2 admission is enabled by the development profile cfg in main.rs; the raw switch activates the incoming root before Context::switch saves the outgoing context on AArch64/x86_64. Snapshot capture/restore is ungated, writer/reader disagree on checksum + layout, and no all-hart quiescence exists.
